title: observability-pipeline-debug-notes-wip-3
content:
Goal: capture breadcrumbs + commands tried for the 2026-03-01 metrics/traces/log ingestion degradation. Personal scratchpad - messy, chronological. Hypotheses and next steps at bottom.

Summary / Impact:
- From ~2026-03-01 09:10 UTC we saw a sharp drop in trace ingestion for hosted-api region-us-west-2. Traces dropped ~85% and some metrics (request_latency_histogram/count) also stopped updating for a subset of services. Logs for affected services continued to appear, but the log-ingest pipeline reported consumer lag and 'dropped records' metrics.
- Affected components: otel-collector (deployment: observability/otel-collector), kafka topic 'ingest.traces.v1', log-ingest consumers (filebeat -> kafka), metrics-pusher job.

Timeline & breadcrumbs:
- 2026-03-01 08:45 UTC: deploy of config change to otel-collector (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/otel-collector-config/pull/42). Change: tweak batching/timeout defaults (batch_size 200 -> 500, timeout_ms 500 -> 1500).
- 2026-03-01 09:05 UTC: increase in 429s from downstream storage (trace-store) observed in logs, spike in exporter retries.
- 2026-03-01 09:10 UTC: Grafana alert - 'Trace ingestion dropped > 70%' fired.
- 2026-03-01 09:12 UTC: noticed consumer lag on kafka partition for ingest.traces.v1.
- 2026-03-01 09:30 UTC: rolled back otel-collector config to previous batching values in staging, but prod rollback delayed until 09:50 UTC. After rollback partial recovery by 10:10 UTC but persistent tail of dropped traces.

Commands run (most useful outputs/snippets):
- kubectl -n observability get pods -l app=otel-collector
  OUTPUT: 3/3 running but restartCount on pod otel-collector-2 shows 1 (restart at 2026-03-01T09:07:23Z).

- kubectl -n observability logs deploy/otel-collector --since=2h | egrep -i 'error|warn|drop|retry' -n
  SAMPLE: 2026-03-01T09:06:58Z WARN exporter/queue 'queue full' dropped 128 spans. exporter=zipkin endpoint=https://trace-store.prod.internal:443
  SAMPLE: 2026-03-01T09:07:05Z ERROR exporter/http 'transport error' tls: handshake failure

- kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka-prod:9092 --describe --group trace-consumer-group
  OUTPUT: LAG on topic ingest.traces.v1 partition 4: 124012 messages. consumer lag increasing between 09:05-09:25.

- curl -sS -X POST https://trace-store.prod.internal/v1/ingest -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d @sample-trace.json -v
  HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
  < Retry-After: 2
  * Connection #0 to host trace-store.prod.internal left intact

- prometheus query (PromQL): rate(otel_exporter_queued_dropped_total[5m])
  RESULT: spike ~09:06-09:12, value ~1.2e3/s (was <1/s baseline).

- elasticsearch / log index checks: GET /_cat/indices?v | grep ingest-logs
  INDEX ingest-logs-2026.03.01 OPEN 1 1 24 0 54mb
  No obvious index growth issue.

Error snippets seen in logs (copied verbatim):
- 'WARN exporter/queue queue full; dropped 128; exporter=zipkin'
- 'ERROR exporter/http transport error: tls: handshake failure'
- 'consumer/commit failed: kafka: leader not available for partition 4'
- 'otelcol/exporter retrying send: status=429 body=\'quota exceeded\''

Initial hypotheses (ranked):
1) Batching config change in otel-collector increased memory/queue pressure, leading to larger bursts sent to trace-store which then returned 429/503 (quota/backpressure) -> exporter queue filled -> local drops and retries -> increased kafka lag as filebeat/kafka producers also backed up.
2) TLS handshake failures indicate intermittent cert or client auth issue between otel-collector and trace-store. Could be unrelated but timing aligns with increased retries. Check cert rotation around 2026-03-01 08:30-09:00.
3) Kafka leader election instability ('leader not available') causing partitions to be temporarily unavailable; combined with backpressure this amplified lag.
4) Network policy or egress throttling (cloud provider) causing intermittent errors.

Checks already performed (and results):
- Rolled back batching change in otel-collector in prod (09:50) -> partial recovery but never to baseline full throughput. Suggests config contributed but not sole cause.
- Checked cert rotation: no automated KMS rotation scheduled at that time, but manual cert push to trace-store happened 2026-02-28 23:00 by infra team (asked infra to confirm).
- Kafka cluster health: controllers stable; noticed 1 leader re-election at 09:03 due to broker transient OOM (investigating with infra). Broker logs show GC pause around 09:02-09:05.
- Checked disk pressure on otel-collector nodes: /var/lib/collector queue used ~68% (ok).

Reproduced quick test locally (staging):
- Using staging otel-collector with batch_size=500 timeout_ms=1500 and trace-store-staging limited to low QPS - observed faster queue fill and local dropped spans consistent with prod logs.

Immediate mitigations attempted:
- Rollback batching change (completed 09:50) -> reduced rate of dropped spans but didn't clear kafka lag.
- Throttled producers via temp rate-limit on service-side (deploy change 10:05) -> reduced incoming rate to otel-collector and allowed slow drain.

Open / next steps (ordered):
- [ ] Confirm infra findings on Kafka broker OOM and leader re-election (assigned: Marco) -> Jira JIRA-OBS-987. Need broker GC logs and heap settings.
- [ ] Verify TLS certs on trace-store and otel-collector clients (assigned: Evelyn). Check if any push/rotation occurred between 2026-02-28 and 2026-03-01.
- [ ] Increase exporter queue capacity temporarily and enable exponential backoff jitter to avoid synchronized bursts (small config change) -> test in staging with soak.
- [ ] Add Prometheus alerts for otelcol queue fill percentage + exporter TLS handshake failures (new alert rule).
- [ ] Create a playbook step: when trace-store returns 429, instead of immediate retry, reduce batch size and add randomized retry window to spread load.
- [ ] Investigate whether filebeat/fluentd producers are batching too aggressively after otel changes (check producers' backpressure handling).

Notes / random observations:
- The timing of Kafka broker GC pause (09:02-09:05) lines up with the first exporter queue full warnings at 09:06. Possible domino: slow broker -> leader election -> producers block -> backlog on producer clients -> burst when back up -> larger batch -> trace-store overloaded.
- We saw one instance of 'tls: handshake failure' which could be transient during broker flapping (if any sidecar proxy renegotiation happened). Need to correlate with kube-proxy / envoy logs.

Immediate temp playbook (for on-call):
1) Check otel-collector pods for restartCount and logs: kubectl -n observability logs deploy/otel-collector --since=30m | egrep -i 'queue full|drop|handshake|retry'
2) If queue full spikes: roll back batching change or reduce batch_size to 100 and timeout_ms to 500.
3) If TLS handshake failures visible: rotate to backup endpoint (trace-store-alt) if available and escalate infra.
4) If kafka lag > 50k: ask infra to check broker GC and consider temporarily increasing consumer parallelism for trace-consumers.

What I'll do next (me, Aisha):
- Continue collecting broker GC logs and correlate with otel logs (today).
- Draft small config change to otel-collector to add jittered backoff and propose to ops (PR draft).
- Add a Grafana panel that overlays exporter_queued_dropped + kafka_consumer_lag for quick triage.

References / links (internal):
- JIRA: JIRA-OBS-987 (broker investigation)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/otel-collector-config/pull/42 (batching change)
- Confluence draft: CONFLUENCE-1234 (incident timeline docs)

End of notes.
